title: Acute Silica Exposure Triggers Pulmonary Inflammation Through Macrophage Pyroptosis: An Experimental Simulation.
authors: Yin, Haoyu; Fang, Lei; Wang, Lifeng; Xia, Yu; Tian, Jiaqi; Ma, Lan; Zhang, Jing; Li, Ning; Li, Weixiu; Yao, Sanqiao; Zhang, Lin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究二氧化硅暴露诱导巨噬细胞焦亡及肺部炎症机制，属纯湿实验与动物模型，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Silica is an essential substrate of various materials, and inhaling silica induces pulmonary diseases potentially associated with macrophage pyroptosis. Utilizing silica of micro- and nano- sizes, we explored the role of macrophage pyroptosis in silica-induced pulmonary inflammation. Under the transmission electron microscopy, we found that the internalization of silica nanoparticle induced membrane rupture and increased the number of intracellular vacuoles, and both sizes of silica could suppress cell viability and proliferation. Also, silica-exposed macrophages generated higher levels of ROS, together with the upregulated expression of NLRP3, ASC, Caspase-1, GSDMD, IL-1beta, and IL-6. However, the expression of these proteins was suppressed after removing ROS or NLRP3. In addition, we found increased expression of TLR4 and NF-kappaB responsible for silica recognition and pyroptosis priming after silica exposure. For in vivo studies, we established animal model by intratracheally instilling 5 mg of silica into mice with/without NLRP3 inhibition. Four weeks later, we found diffused infiltration of inflammatory cells and enhanced collagen hyperplasia partially reversed by additional treatment with MCC950, so as the expression of pyroptotic molecules and proinflammatory cytokines. In particular, the dual immunofluorescent staining showed co-expression of macrophage-specific biomarker F4/80 and NLRP3 within the cells, and silica of nano-size showed more potent toxicity and pathogenicity than that of the micro-sized particles both in vitro and in vivo. To sum up, macrophage pyroptosis is an upstream event of silica-induced pulmonary inflammation promoted by ROS through the TLR4/NLRP3/NF-kappaB signaling axis.
abstract_zh: 二氧化硅是多种材料的重要基底，吸入二氧化硅可诱发肺部疾病，这可能与巨噬细胞焦亡（macrophage pyroptosis）相关。利用微米和纳米尺寸的二氧化硅，我们探讨了巨噬细胞焦亡在二氧化硅诱导的肺部炎症中的作用。在透射电子显微镜下，我们发现二氧化硅纳米颗粒的内化诱导了膜破裂并增加了细胞内空泡的数量，且两种尺寸的二氧化硅均能抑制细胞活力和增殖。此外，暴露于二氧化硅的巨噬细胞产生了更高水平的ROS，同时NLRP3、ASC、Caspase-1、GSDMD、IL-1beta和IL-6的表达上调。然而，在去除ROS或NLRP3后，这些蛋白的表达受到抑制。另外，我们发现二氧化硅暴露后，负责二氧化硅识别和焦亡启动的TLR4和NF-kappaB表达增加。在体内研究中，我们通过气管内滴注5 mg二氧化硅建立动物模型，小鼠伴有或不伴有NLRP3抑制。四周后，我们发现炎症细胞的弥漫性浸润和胶原增生增强，这些现象部分被额外使用MCC950治疗所逆转，焦亡分子和促炎细胞因子的表达也是如此。特别地，双重免疫荧光染色显示巨噬细胞特异性生物标志物F4/80和NLRP3在细胞内的共表达，且纳米尺寸的二氧化硅在体外和体内均显示出比微米颗粒更强的毒性和致病性。总之，巨噬细胞焦亡是二氧化硅诱导的肺部炎症的上游事件，由ROS通过TLR4/NLRP3/NF-kappaB信号轴促进。
